anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have their secondary ground pins (GND2, pin 5) connected to the common GND net, the same net as their primary grounds (GND1, pin 4).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the board implements two isolated CAN buses through isolated CAN transceivers. In standard use of an isolated CAN transceiver, GND2 must be kept isolated from GND1/GND (or connected to a separate isolated CAN ground) to preserve galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The intended galvanic isolation of the CAN interfaces is defeated; the buses share the same ground reference as the CM4 side, which can cause ground loops and makes the board behave differently from the intended isolated CAN architecture.

parsed.summary: The clearest deviation is that the supposedly isolated CAN transceivers have their secondary grounds tied to the common GND net, contradicting the intended isolated CAN buses.
